top_stories.title: Critical Microsoft Entra ID vulnerability exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-69836)
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-69836) in Microsoft Entra ID, its cloud identity and access management service, with a maximum CVSS score of 10.0. The flaw, discovered by Microsoft Principal Security Engineer Robert Fitzpatrick, allows an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute code and has been confirmed as exploited in the wild.

top_stories.title: Microsoft patches max severity code execution, privilege escalation flaws
top_stories.summary: Microsoft patched a maximum-severity vulnerability in its Entra ID IAM platform that has been actively exploited in attacks. The flaw involves code execution and privilege escalation, representing a critical security risk to organizations using Microsoft's identity and access management platform.

top_stories.title: Citrix urges customers to fix critical NetScaler authentication bypass (CVE-2026-19490)
top_stories.summary: Citrix has patched a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-19490) in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, urging immediate upgrades. The flaw affects NetScaler Gateway, a widely deployed remote access and SSO solution, making it directly relevant to authentication and access management infrastructure.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Patches Severe Entra ID Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Allowing Remote Code Execution
top_stories.summary: Microsoft patched a critical vulnerability in Microsoft Entra ID with a CVSS score of 10.0 that could allow remote code execution. Microsoft initially marked the flaw as exploited before correcting that status to "No" following press inquiry.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Fixes 'Perfect 10' Exploit That Could Have Let Hackers Run Code Remotely
top_stories.summary: Microsoft patched a critical severity (CVSS 10.0) remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft Entra ID before publicly disclosing the CVE. Microsoft reports no evidence of exploitation in the wild prior to the patch being applied.

news.title: Microsoft’s CVSS 10.0 Entra ID RCE Briefly Tagged ‘Exploited’ Before Correction — and What That Reveals About Identity Infrastructure Disclosure
news.summary: Microsoft disclosed CVE-2026-69836, a CVSS 10.0 remote code execution vulnerability in Entra ID, representing an unauthenticated, network-accessible attack vector into the identity platform. The vulnerability was briefly and incorrectly tagged as actively exploited before the designation was corrected, raising questions about disclosure accuracy for critical identity infrastructure.

news.title: Hundreds of leaked AWS keys give full control over corporate accounts
news.summary: Over 9,300 AWS access keys publicly exposed between August 2022 and August 2026 have been found to still be active and valid. The leaked credentials grant full control over corporate AWS accounts, representing a significant credential and access management security failure.

news.title: Nearly half of enterprises have no one leading PQC migration
news.summary: A new Axiad report finds that nearly half of enterprises lack designated ownership for post-quantum cryptography migration despite believing they are prepared for quantum security challenges. The research highlights gaps in governance around cryptographic asset inventory, including certificates, cryptographic keys, and algorithms needed before PQC migration can be planned.

news.title: Suspected Russian Hackers Abuse Google OAuth and WhatsApp Linking to Hijack Accounts
news.summary: Three suspected Russian cyber espionage groups (UNC6293, UNC7005, and UNC5976) have been observed abusing legitimate Google OAuth and WhatsApp account-linking authentication flows to hijack accounts. The attacks target individuals in academia, aerospace and defense, governments, and think tanks across Europe and the U.S.

news.title: Fine-Grained Access Control Now Available for All Heroku Customers
news.summary: Heroku has made Fine-Grained Access Controls (FGAC) generally available to all customers. The new system replaces predefined roles (admin, member, collaborator) with individual capability-based permissions, giving administrators more granular control over user access.

news.title: Microsoft sounds alarm as perfect-10 Entra ID flaw comes under attack
news.summary: Microsoft has disclosed a critical perfect-10 (CVSS 10.0) vulnerability in Microsoft Entra ID that has been actively exploited. The cloud identity flaw has been patched by Microsoft, though the company has not disclosed details about the threat actors involved or the scope of exploitation.

news.title: N-able Bug Exposes Password Vault Master Keys
news.summary: A vulnerability in N-able's Passportal password manager exposed master keys to the password vault. The flaw affects MSPs and SMBs who use the cloud-based product, and concerns remain about residual risk even after patching due to the cloud architecture.

news.title: AWS limits AI agents’ data access, even when manipulated
news.summary: AWS has introduced an approach for propagating user authorization context through AI agents in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, enabling access controls to be enforced at the infrastructure level rather than relying on the agent itself. The system ensures that AI agents accessing DynamoDB tables, document repositories, SaaS platforms, and internal knowledge bases respect user-level permissions even when the agent is manipulated.

news.title: Critical NetScaler Flaw Can Bypass Authentication on Certain Gateway and AAA Servers
news.summary: Citrix has released security updates addressing two vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, including a critical-severity authentication bypass flaw. The vulnerability affects customer-managed deployments including certain FIPS and NDcPP builds, as well as SecurAccess configurations on Gateway and AAA servers.

news.title: Why "Shady AI" is Security's Next Big Governance Problem
news.summary: A Meta AI agent caused a Sev 1 security incident in March 2026 when it publicly posted a response containing sensitive company and user data that was visible to unauthorized employees. The incident highlights authorization and access control failures in AI agent workflows, where AI systems can bypass intended access boundaries.

news.title: Cloudflare Workers Spectre Attack Leaks JWT From Co-Located Worker at 12 Bits/Second
news.summary: Researchers demonstrated a remote Spectre side-channel attack against Cloudflare Workers that successfully leaked a JSON Web Token (JWT) from a co-located Worker at up to 12 bits per second in a production environment. The attack represents a 360x speed improvement over a similar 2021 demonstration, targeting JWTs which are widely used for authentication and authorization in modern applications.

news.title: jumpserver v4.10.19
news.summary: JumpServer released version 4.10.19 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. JumpServer provides DevOps and IT teams with secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, database, and RemoteApp endpoints via a web browser.

news.title: Pathlock Recognized as an Overall Leader in the 2026 KuppingerCole Analysts Leadership Compass for Identity and Access Governance
news.summary: Pathlock has been recognized as an Overall Leader in the 2026 KuppingerCole Analysts Leadership Compass for Identity and Access Governance. The report specifically noted that high-risk access governance is one of Pathlock's stronger areas, positioning the company within the converged identity governance and ERP security market.

news.title: Hackers Compromised 14,500+ Dahua Devices Using Credential Attacks, Auth Bypasses, and P2P
news.summary: Researchers at Hunt.io documented a campaign called Operation CameraSwarm that compromised over 14,530 Dahua IoT devices between June and July 2026 using credential attacks and two authentication-bypass vulnerabilities. The attack leveraged weak credentials, auth-bypass flaws, and P2P relay techniques against internet-exposed security cameras.

news.title: Cyera's Oasis Security Buy Is All About AI Agent Control
news.summary: Cyera acquired Oasis Security in a $1 billion deal to combine data security and identity management into a unified control plane. The acquisition redefines privileged access management around business context and dynamic AI agent identities rather than static roles.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian cybercriminal Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved unauthorized access to Snowflake customer accounts, largely enabled by stolen credentials and lack of MFA enforcement.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem report on a data breach in which a contractor accidentally published dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, to a public GitHub repository. The credentials remained exposed for nearly six months before KrebsOnSecurity notified the agency, highlighting gaps in secrets management and credential monitoring practices.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise organizational accounts.
